no-history-read: no history was read: this is not a git repository
history-before: history was not read before the clone's first commit
feature-code-on-a-file: a feature file already has the feature code
not-a-feature-code: {given}: this is not a feature code, two to five uppercase letters or digits
unknown-feature-code: no feature file has the feature code {featureCode}; the feature files have {featureCodes}
unreadable-in-tree: allocate could not read {path}, and gives no code: {said}
unreadable-history: allocate could not read the repository's history, and gives no code: {said}
damaged-repository: allocate could not read the repository, and gives no code: {said}
feature-file-does-not-parse: allocate could not read the feature file {file}, which does not parse, and gives no code
report-not-written: a report could not be written to {place}: {why}
more-than-one-to-stdout: more than one report would go to standard output, and at most one may: {reports}
outputs-share-file: two reports would go in one file: {reports}
output-overwrites-input: a report would overwrite {file}, a file the run reads
unknown-flag: {command} does not take the flag {flag}; see {help}
missing-value: the flag {flag} is missing its value; see {help}
unwanted-value: the flag {flag} takes no value, and was given {value}; see {help}
stray-argument: {argument} is no flag and no flag's value; see {help}
repeated-flag: the flag {flag} may be given only once; see {help}
equals-form: {given} joins a flag and its value with an equals sign; write it {spelling}; see {help}
flag-before-command: the flag {flag} goes after the command; see {help}
unknown-format: spec-controller does not write the report format {format}; it writes {formats}; see {help}
no-feature-code: allocate needs a feature code; see {help}
extra-argument: allocate takes one feature code, and {argument} is past it; see {help}
command-balance: reconcile the claims in the feature files against the evidence that ran
command-allocate: give the next free claim code for a feature code
flag-features: the folder of feature files, read at any depth (default: features)
flag-pytest: a pytest JUnit XML evidence report
flag-junit: a JUnit XML evidence report, or a folder of them
flag-ci-steps: the CI run's record of its steps
flag-target: the name of the project reconciled, for the provenance
flag-source-sha: the commit reconciled, for the provenance (default: HEAD)
flag-format: a report's format, md or json, and after a colon the file it goes to; repeatable
flag-strict: read every claim as if nothing were put off
flag-new: the feature code is new: give its first claim code
